findings.title: Generic SVG selector can falsely certify that sample data rendered
findings.what: The test claims to prove that each curated view rendered a populated table or chart, but DATA_SURFACE is `table tbody tr, svg`. Any SVG within main—including a PatternFly icon or other decorative UI graphic—makes the count positive. A parser or sample-shape regression that removes the primary chart can therefore pass while only incidental SVG remains, so the emitted evidence is not specific or reproducible evidence of the claimed data surface.
findings.fix: Replace the bare `svg` arm with a stable chart-specific locator or test attribute applied to actual populated chart roots; keep `table tbody tr` for populated tables and assert the matched element is outside empty-state/decorative UI containers.
findings.acceptance: For every DATA_VIEWS route, the test passes with its populated table/chart present and fails after replacing the primary data surface with an empty state while leaving ordinary SVG icons in main; the selector contains no unqualified `svg` arm.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarially re-read the detector definition and its sole assertion at baseline c8b98a29508b5eb7725c75a7e2a41dfa94c1feba. Lines 34-36 explicitly equate any SVG with a chart, and lines 91-95 require only a positive aggregate count; there is no chart ownership, data-bearing attribute, role, or decorative-SVG exclusion. The candidate is therefore a concrete false-negative in this file, independent of undocumented implementation details.
